name: Distillation Tower
notes: Variable height in GT (3 to 12 blocks); shown at height 5, which gives 4 output layers (enough for oil distillation). All blocks are Clean Stainless Steel Machine Casings (at least 7 x height - 5 = 30 here). Bottom layer: solid 3x3 with the controller in the front centre; it takes the input hatch, input and output buses, energy and maintenance. Every layer above the bottom is a ring around an air core and needs at least one output hatch of its own: output number N goes to the hatches on layer N+1, so the planner places one output hatch on every layer (regions layer1 to layer4). The top layer is closed with a casing in its centre. Ring casings also take energy and maintenance. Output hatches on the rings may not face up or down (GT disallowOnly(UP, DOWN)); the planner never turns them that way. GT does not allow the tower to be rotated or flipped. Sharing: GT5u adds every hatch it finds during the structure check to each controller whose structure contains it, so a shared wall can carry one output hatch per layer for two towers. Only do that when both towers run the same recipe, because each layer receives a different fluid. Energy and maintenance are never marked shareable (energy starvation; maintenance flags are cleared by the first reader).
